app.repair.detail:
Repair tries these in order, from least to most costly:

1. Cold-boot the VM (without the snapshot) and wait for the network — no data is affected
2. Only if that fails, reset Android data — the app list is kept and apps reinstall when opened,
   but in-app sign-ins and viewing history will be lost

Only the current AVD is affected; the system image and this PC's APK cache are untouched. The whole process takes about 1–5 minutes. Continue?

guide.step1: Boot menu: Use ↓ to select Installation - Install Android-x86 to harddisk, then press Enter
guide.step2: Choose Partition: Select Create/Modify partitions; when asked whether to use GPT, select No
guide.step3: cfdisk partitioning: New → Primary → press Enter to accept the size → Bootable → Write → type yes → Quit
guide.step4: Format: Select vda1 → when prompted to format, select ext4 → Yes
guide.step5: Bootloader & system: For Install GRUB select Yes; for Install /system as read-write select Yes
guide.step6: Finish: When progress reaches 100%, click “I've finished installing” below (ApkStart will restart and take over automatically)
guide.sub: The VM window is open. Follow these 6 steps once; afterwards ApkStart boots straight from the disk and no longer needs the image.
guide.tip: If you later see a message that adb is not connected: in the VM window press Ctrl+Alt+F1 to open a terminal, run setprop service.adb.tcp.port 5555, stop adbd, start adbd, then press Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical interface.

settings.aboutDesc: A Windows Android app launcher that installs on double-click: APK installation, desktop shortcuts, running in separate windows, and two-way file sharing.
settings.aboutWechatTip: Scan to follow the official account
settings.adbPathPlaceholder: Leave empty to search PATH / the Android SDK automatically
settings.advancedParams: Advanced parameters (usually no need to change)
settings.airplaneDesc: Cuts the network completely (including mobile data); turn on when you need quiet.
settings.androidGroup: Android system settings (no need to open the Android desktop)
settings.androidStatusDesc: Turns off system animations, lifts the background process limit, and adds the current app to the battery whitelist — the most noticeable improvement on low-end PCs.
settings.animationsDesc: Turning this off makes UI transitions noticeably faster, with no effect on features.
settings.applyNote: Settings take effect immediately after being changed
settings.associateApkDesc: Double-click an APK to install it straight into ApkStart (written for the current user only, no administrator needed)
settings.audioDesc: Lets app notification sounds and video audio play normally. Turn off only if you need no sound at all and want to save a little more CPU.
settings.autoMirrorDesc: When a direct GitHub connection is too slow, it also speed-tests ghfast.top / gh-proxy.com, two public forwarding services (they only forward public release files; no account is involved). Turn this off to use only direct connections and your own prefix.
settings.autoProfileDesc: Memory, core count, rendering backend, port, and acceleration are all chosen automatically; if startup fails it retries with lower settings — no manual changes needed.
settings.autoShortcut: Create a desktop shortcut automatically after install
settings.autoShortcutDesc: Shortcuts carry the real app icon; double-click to go straight into the app
settings.autoStart: Start automatically at boot (on by default)
settings.autoStartDesc: Stays in the tray after you sign in to Windows, so double-clicking a desktop icon opens apps instantly — no manual launch needed.
settings.avdDir: Android data folder (apps, games, and quick-boot snapshots)
settings.avdDirDesc: This is what really eats disk: the data partition (6 GB by default, expandable above) + quick-boot snapshots (about 2–3 GB). If disk space is tight, point it at another drive (e.g. D:) and restart the app to apply; the apkstart.avd folder in the old location can be moved over wholesale and then deleted.
settings.avdDirPlaceholder: Default: the avd folder under the runtime folder
settings.cleanLeftoversTitle: Scan for and remove program folders left by old versions, stale uninstall entries, and update temp files
settings.cleanSnapshotsToo: Also clear the current AVD's quick-boot snapshots (the runtime is stopped first, so several GB of snapshots can actually be reclaimed)
settings.compatImageDesc: There is now a single universal Android 14 image that runs both x86 and ARM apps; it downloads automatically the first time an ARM app is encountered, with no manual switching. This switch exists only for compatibility with old configurations.
settings.connectionsDesc: Large files are downloaded in parallel chunks. The default 8 threads already saturate most home broadband connections; on a stable network you can try 16.
settings.dataSize: Android データパーティション (apps and games go here)
settings.deepTrimDesc: Additionally disables background packages such as the Play Store, Setup Wizard, and print services, keeping only what's needed to open apps. If an app complains that Google Play services are missing, turning this off restores them automatically.
settings.desktopGroup: デスクトップとアプリ
settings.diagnosticsNote: The diagnostics report is for troubleshooting; rebuilding restores desktop + Start menu entries
settings.diskUsage: Total disk usage (runtime + Android data + cache)
settings.diskUsageDesc: The system image is shared machine-wide as a single copy, and app data is stored in a differencing layer; old images, old snapshots, logs, and lock files can all be reclaimed. Logs rotate automatically past a size cap and never grow without limit. “Reset Android data” really deletes several GB of user data, keeping only the system itself.
settings.displayFullscreen: Fullscreen (fills the screen, keeps the phone aspect ratio with black bars)
settings.displayModeDesc: Press F11 at any time or use the tray menu to switch; fullscreen only enlarges the window without changing the aspect ratio, and switching does not restart the app.
settings.displayWindow: Portrait window (freely resizable, remembers each app's size)
settings.engineAttach: Connect to an existing runtime (advanced: reuse the adb port of WSA / another emulator)
settings.engineBuiltin: Built-in runtime (recommended, QEMU + Android-x86, no third-party dependencies)
settings.fastDnsDesc: Assigns public DNS in China (Alibaba / Tencent) to Android. By default Android uses the host's DNS; if the host is on a VPN or a corporate network, resolution can take hundreds of milliseconds and video apps are slow to load their first screen. Turn this off if intranet domains stop resolving correctly.
settings.fileSharingNote: The two folders stay in two-way sync continuously; files an Android app saves to that folder appear in the local shared folder.
settings.giteeTokenDesc: This project's repository is public, so Gitee's release list is readable anonymously and the Gitee source works with this left empty. Fill it in only if “Gitee is rate-limiting you (returns 403/429)” or you want to read a private branch: gitee.com → Settings → Personal access tokens, check only “projects”. It is only used to read the release list and uploads nothing.
settings.giteeTokenPlaceholder: Can be left empty: public repos are readable anonymously
settings.growDataNote: Expansion happens in place: installed apps and save data are kept; the next app launch just takes a few extra seconds.
settings.keepSnapshotDesc: The second launch of an app takes only a few seconds; the cost is an extra ram.bin of about 2–3 GB on disk. If disk space is tight you can turn this off: it only affects startup speed, not apps or save data.
settings.languageDesc: Interface language for ApkStart. "Auto" follows your Windows display language.
settings.liteModeDesc: Tightens the vCPU quota and lowers process priority so the CPU yields to the Windows desktop first. The “Resource policy” above already sets this automatically.
settings.mirrorPrefix: Download mirror prefix (optional, speeds up GitHub)
settings.mirrorPrefixDesc: If filled in, only your prefix is used and the two public mirrors above are no longer tried; if left empty, the “Auto” logic decides. The downloader prepends it to the real URL.
settings.mouseLeftDesc: The emulator treats the left button as a finger tap natively; press and drag to swipe — no extra setup needed.
settings.mouseNote: The mappings above apply only while an app window is in the foreground; back on the desktop or after closing the window, the mouse behaves exactly as native Windows again.
settings.mouseRightBackDesc: By default the emulator also treats the right button as a tap (easy to trigger by accident). When enabled, the right button only goes Back and no longer taps.
settings.mouseSide: Mouse side buttons · Back / Forward (off by default)
settings.mouseSideDesc: Side-button mapping needs a global mouse hook. The hook is installed only while an ApkStart app window is in the foreground and is removed immediately on focus loss or close, so it never slows down your desktop.
settings.mouseWheelDesc: Smooth mode merges scrolling within a short window into a single swipe gesture, avoiding notch-by-notch judder and not spawning an adb process for every notch.
settings.perfNote: The Android environment boots only once and stays resident; afterwards, opening an app no longer reruns the whole system — it just starts that app and stops other app processes. Closing the last window clears background apps and parks the container, and the next launch is still instant.
settings.portraitSizeDesc: In window mode you can drag the edges to resize freely; this sets Android's internal rendering size — smaller is lighter on performance.
settings.prewarmDesc: Right after ApkStart starts, it boots the Android environment in the background (the window stays hidden the whole time — you'll never see the emulator). After that, opening any app is a single “open” step; measured startup drops from 20+ seconds to almost no wait. The cost is about 1 GB of memory held while idle; turn it off and the first app launch needs a cold start.
settings.priorityBalanced: Balanced (recommended) · Runtime yields to foreground windows
settings.priorityGame: Gaming / low latency · Runtime at high priority, good for FPS and rhythm games
settings.priorityModeDesc: Gaming mode keeps the Android VM at a higher CPU priority and reduces host-side polling for the lowest input and display latency; the cost is that other programs on the PC get slower. With no app window open, the container still lowers its priority and parks automatically.
settings.priorityPerformance: Performance first · Runtime at the same priority as the foreground
settings.rebuildShortcutsNote: If desktop icons were deleted by mistake or blocked by security software, click here to restore them all per the current settings.
settings.repairNetworkTitle: When the Android VM has no network (web pages in apps stay black or keep spinning), use this to reset the Android data to fix networking. Your app list is kept, and apps reinstall automatically when opened
settings.resetDataTitle: Erase the Android /data user data, installed apps, and quick-boot snapshots, restoring a clean just-installed state
settings.resourceBalanced: Balanced · Half the physical cores / yields to foreground / 720p (recommended)
settings.resourceModeDesc: Decides how much CPU the Android VM gets and how detailed the picture is. If Hongguo/Douyin stutter, switch to “Smooth”; if you just keep small apps running in the background, switch to “Power saving”. Takes effect the next time you open an app.
settings.resourceSave: Power saving · 2 cores / yields to foreground / 540p (old PCs, background use)
settings.resourceSmooth: Smooth · Unlimited cores / same priority as foreground (video, games)
settings.runtimeDir: Runtime data folder (system image · installed apps · snapshots)
settings.runtimeDirDesc: This uses the most space (several GB). Moving it to a non-system drive greatly relieves pressure on drive C; a restart is required after changing it, and existing data is not moved automatically (copy it manually, then delete the old folder).
settings.runtimeDirPlaceholder: Default: user data folder on drive C
settings.setupAdvanced: Advanced: connect to an existing runtime
settings.setupNote: Fully automatic: no image to pick, no acceleration to enable, no memory to tune
settings.sharedDirDesc: After a change, existing files in the old folder are moved to the new one automatically; file sharing that is currently running is unaffected.
settings.shortcutDir: ショートカットフォルダー
settings.sourceGitee: Gitee のみ (usually fastest in China)
settings.sourcePref: 更新とダウンロードソース
settings.sourcePrefDesc: “Auto” asks both GitHub and Gitee for the latest version, actually downloads 256 KB from each download URL to test its speed, then downloads from the fastest one; if one source is unreachable, updates still work.
settings.startMenuShortcut: Also add to the Start menu
settings.startMenuShortcutDesc: Windows Search can find apps by name, and the taskbar groups by app too
settings.stopRuntime: 内蔵の VM を停止
settings.systemImagePlaceholder: Path to an Android-x86 / Bliss OS ISO or IMG; leave empty to use the default location

settings.uninstall: ApkStart をアンインストール

settings.uninstallNote: Uninstalling removes the .apk association and the program; for the portable edition, delete the folder manually as instructed.
settings.updateNote: Gets the latest version from GitHub (RoutineMiku/apkstart); the lightweight edition downloads the portable package and replaces the program files automatically, without affecting the runtime, installed apps, or snapshots.
settings.wheelNative: Native · Let the emulator handle each notch
settings.wheelSmooth: Smooth (recommended) · Merge multiple scrolls into one fluid swipe
settings.wifiDesc: The wireless network inside the Android VM; turning it off saves a little CPU.
